Plan, run and report survey research

Design your questionnaire, plan your analysis and prepare an APA 7 report. Work visually in SurveyStudio or use R.

For people conducting, supervising, reviewing or planning survey research.

Explore templates Get started

SurveyStudio opens through R. The setup guide explains installing the required software and opening your first study.

Conducting a survey for your studies?

Plan your research, create your questionnaire, analyse responses and prepare your report. Guidance for survey students

Supervising students conducting survey research?

Review each student’s analysis plan, compare it with the completed report and follow recorded amendments and their reasons. Guidance for supervisors

Reviewing a survey study as an ethics committee?

Examine the proposed study documentation, then review the completed study and its recorded changes. Guidance for ethics committees

Planning survey research for an NGO or research organisation?

Prepare a pre-analysis plan and keep the questionnaire, analysis decisions and reporting connected. Guidance for NGOs and research organisations

Keep your questionnaire and analysis plan connected

Save your questions, scoring rules, analysis plan and references in a portable .sframe file. Collect responses using your chosen setup, check their quality and prepare a report that presents the planned analyses alongside the results and your interpretation.

Record later changes with their reasons so readers can follow the study’s development.

Plan your study before collecting responses. Record your research questions, hypotheses and analysis choices alongside the questionnaire. How to write the analysis plan.

Move from responses to a research report. Check the collected responses, run the planned analyses and prepare APA 7 tables, figures and references for supported methods. See the report stage.

Keep a record of your research design. Preserve the questionnaire version, sources and disclosed amendments with the design file. Verify a .sframe file to check that it matches the hash recorded when it was saved.

For example, start with the course evaluation survey, plan how you will summarise the ratings, collect responses and prepare a report for the teaching team. It is an example to adapt to your own course and questions.

Start from a template

Each template holds a questionnaire and an example analysis plan to adapt to your own study.

Psychology and measurement. Likert scale questionnaire, Measurement model questionnaire (CFA and SEM).

Education. Course evaluation survey, Training evaluation before and after.

Business. Customer satisfaction survey, Employee engagement survey, Supplier and venue selection (decision making).

Events and tourism. Open-ended feedback survey.

Research methods. Pilot survey with a small sample, Preparing a survey study for preregistration.

All questionnaire templates

How a study runs

  1. Design the questionnaire and write the analysis plan, with hypotheses and decision rules, before collecting responses.
  2. Collect responses with a survey web page, stored where you choose, such as a Google Sheet you own.
  3. Check responses for failed attention checks, speeding, identical answers across a scale and missing answers.
  4. Analyse the responses with the plan as written. A later change is recorded as an amendment with its reason.
  5. Report in APA 7, as HTML, Word, PDF or OpenDocument.

Run a study in SurveyStudio shows each stage by point and click, and Run a study in R shows the same stages in R.

Already use R? Open a first study from the Console 
install.packages("surveyframe")
library(surveyframe)
d <- sframe_demo("first_survey")

Then read the R reference, the worked examples and the changelog.
